title_en: Hachiman Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. and Japan Debao Shipping Co., Ltd. — dispute over cargo damage under a contract of maritime carriage of goods
ruling_gist_en: The carrier under a contract of carriage of goods by sea shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 55 of the Maritime Code of the PRC, bear liability for compensation for cargo damage occurring during the period of its responsibility.

full_text_en:
Hachiman Shipping S.A. v. Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. and Dorval Kaiun K.K. — dispute over cargo damage under contract of carriage of goods by sea

Ruling Summary

The carrier under a contract of carriage of goods by sea shall bear liability for cargo damage occurring during its period of responsibility in accordance with Article 55 of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China.

The actual value of the goods provided for in Article 55 of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China does not include loss from market price fluctuations.

Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial Judgment No. 6 (2013)

Reapplying Petitioner (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hachiman Shipping S.A. Address: 53rd Street, Urbanizacion Obarrio, Torre Swiss Bank, 16th Floor, Panama, Republic of Panama.

Legal Representative: Takashi Aoyama, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Jianfeng, Attorney at Shanghai Office of King & Wood Mallesons.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yi, Paralegal at Shanghai Office of King & Wood Mallesons.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. Address: Room 601, Building 2, No. 4268 Zhennan Road, Jiading District, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Ding Peikun, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Zhensheng, Attorney at Shanghai Panyang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shen Qiuming, Attorney at Shanghai Panyang Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: Dorval Kaiun K.K. Address: 7th Floor, Sumitomo Fudosan Kayabacho Bldg., 16-3, 1-Chome Shinkawa, Chuo-ku, Tokyo, Japan.

Legal Representative: Kaoru Michiura, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Jianfeng, Attorney at Shanghai Office of King & Wood Mallesons.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yi, Paralegal at Shanghai Office of King & Wood Mallesons.

The Reapplying Petitioner Hachiman Shipping S.A. (hereinafter referred to as Hachiman) filed an application for retrial with this Court, disagreeing with the civil judgment (2011) Luminsizhongzi No. 131 rendered by the High People's Court of Shandong Province in the dispute over cargo damage under a contract of carriage of goods by sea with the Respondent Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenfu) and the Defendant at First Instance and Appellant at Second Instance Dorval Kaiun K.K. (hereinafter referred to as Dorval). This Court issued a civil ruling (2012) Minshenzi No. 708 on September 20, 2012, granting retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case. Xu Jianfeng and Chen Yi, the agents ad litem of Hachiman and Dorval, and Chen Zhensheng, the agent ad litem of Shenfu, attended the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

On August 12, 2009, Shenfu filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Maritime Court, alleging that on August 23, 2008, Dorval issued an on-board order bill of lading with number GTHQ-5702. After the subject goods arrived at Qingdao Port, cargo damage was discovered upon inspection. Dorval and Hachiman, as carrier and actual carrier, should be jointly and severally liable for such damage. Based on this, Shenfu filed the lawsuit requesting that Dorval and Hachiman jointly and severally compensate for cargo loss of RMB 8,347,849.57 and interest on that amount (calculated from October 23, 2008, at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for enterprises for the same period and same currency up to the date determined by the judgment), and bear the litigation costs of this case and the expenses incurred by Shenfu for realizing its claims.

Dorval and Hachiman defended, stating: 1. Dorval and Hachiman delivered the goods as recorded in the bill of lading and are not responsible for matters outside the bill of lading in accordance with law; 2. Shenfu did not prove that the change in the color of the phenol was caused by the fault of Dorval or Hachiman; 3. A change in phenol color does not necessarily mean that the phenol was damaged; 4. The amount of loss claimed by Shenfu has no factual or legal basis; 5. Dorval and Hachiman are entitled to limitation of liability for maritime claims. Shenfu's claims have no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed.

The following facts were found by the Qingdao Maritime Court at first instance:

On September 23, 2008, Shenfu entered into a sales contract WZ08Y-00554P/4 with SUMITOMO CORPORATION (HONG KONG) LTD. for the purchase of 1,001.53 tons of phenol. The contract provided for a price term of CFR Qingdao, China, and a maximum phenol color of 10 Hazen. On September 24, 2008, Shenfu applied to the Zhabei Subbranch of the Bank of Shanghai for the issuance of an irrevocable usance documentary letter of credit TF0826837258ILHL in favor of SUMITOMO CORPORATION (HONG KONG) LTD., with a unit price of USD 1,530 per ton and a total letter of credit amount of USD 1,532,340.90. On December 4, 2008, Shenfu paid the letter of credit amount of RMB 10,569,474.59.

This batch of phenol was carried by the Panama-flagged vessel M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY, which was owned by Hachiman. The M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY was an oil/chemical tanker built in 1998, with a deadweight tonnage of 16,465 metric tons, a gross tonnage of 9,599, and a net tonnage of 5,132.

On August 23, 2008, the goods were loaded on board the vessel at the port of Huelva, Spain, and Dorval issued a clean order bill of lading number GTHQ-5702. The bill of lading recorded: Shipper: SUMITOMO DEUTSCHLAND GmbH; Consignee: to order; Notify party: SUMITOMO CORPORATION (SHANGHAI) LTD.; Goods: 1,001.53 tons of phenol; Stowage compartments: 7P, 7S, 10P; Port of discharge: Qingdao, China; Freight prepaid. Shenfu acquired the bill of lading through endorsement by the shipper SUMITOMO DEUTSCHLAND GmbH and accordingly took delivery of the shipped goods at the port of discharge.

Before the goods were loaded, SGS conducted quality and weight inspections of the phenol and issued a weight certificate and a quality certificate. The quality certificate recorded a phenol color of less than 5 Hazen, along with other quality indicators. On November 5, 2008, Shanghai INSPEC Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd. inspected the on-board phenol samples and issued Inspection Report No. OP2008-1501SH-1 for the tank samples (sampled on August 23, 2008), which recorded a phenol color of 5 Hazen after loading.

After the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY departed from the loading port, it berthed at the Mingyang Chemical Dock in Qingdao Port at 16:40 on October 22, 2008. Shanghai Dongfang Tianxiang Inspection Service Co., Ltd., commissioned by Shenfu, conducted joint sampling of the cargo in tanks 7P, 7S, and 10P of the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY, together with Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. (commissioned by the Shanghai Branch of Huatai Insurance Agency & Consultant Service Ltd.), Shanghai Dongfang Surveyors Co., Ltd. (appointed by the cargo insurer), and SGS. On October 23, 2008, the master of the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY issued a statement: "The phenol loaded in tanks 7P and 10P has changed color; the phenol in tank 7S was tested and found to be in good condition. All the above cargo will be mixed and discharged into one shore receiving tank. The liability arising from the mixing shall be borne by the shipowner." On October 24, 2008, at 01:00, the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY commenced discharge, completing discharge at 19:20 on the same day, and all the phenol was mixed and discharged into shore tank T-108. Shanghai Fanhua Tianheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd., commissioned by the Shanghai Branch of Huatai Insurance Agency & Consultant Service Ltd., representing the owner of the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY and its hull insurer, conducted joint sampling of the phenol in shore tank T-108 together with Shanghai Dongfang Tianxiang Inspection Service Co., Ltd., Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd., Shanghai Dongfang Surveyors Co., Ltd., and SGS.

On October 25, 2008, Shanghai Dongfang Tianxiang Inspection Service Co., Ltd. issued Inspection Report No. RH082555, which recorded: The phenol color in tank 7S was 7 Hazen, in tank 7P was 27 Hazen, and in tank 10P was 30 Hazen.

On November 4, 2008, the (Caojing) laboratory of Shanghai INSPEC Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd. tested the relevant samples, with representatives from Shenfu, Shanghai Dongfang Tianxiang Inspection Service Co., Ltd., Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd., Shanghai Dongfang Surveyors Co., Ltd., and Shanghai Fanhua Tianheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. each confirming that the samples were well sealed. On November 5, 2008, Shanghai INSPEC Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd. issued Inspection Reports No. OP2008-1501SH-7, OP2008-1501SH-8, and OP2008-1501SH-9, in addition to Inspection Report No. OP2008-1501SH-1 for the tank samples. On November 7, 2008, it issued Inspection Report No. ZJG0569/08, which respectively recorded: Upon the vessel's arrival at Qingdao Port and before discharge (sampled on October 22, 2008): phenol color in tank 7S was 3 Hazen, in tank 7P was 19 Hazen, and in tank 10P was 21 Hazen; After discharge (sampled on October 24, 2008): phenol color in Qingdao shore tank T-108 was 12 Hazen. Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Fanhua Tianheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. both confirmed the above inspection reports issued by Shanghai INSPEC Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd.

From November 4 to November 17, 2008, Shenfu and Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. sent inquiry letters to five companies including Xiamen Gaote Gaoxin Materials Co., Ltd., offering to sell phenol with a color less than 50 Hazen at a price of RMB 4,750 to 5,000 per ton, but all five companies refused on the grounds that the color exceeded the standard or the price was too high.

On November 27, 2008, Shenfu (as supplier) entered into a product supply and purchase contract with Qingdao Mingyang Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mingyang) (as buyer) for the sale of 1,400 tons of phenol at a price of RMB 4,720 per ton, with an actual transaction of 996 tons and a total price of RMB 4,701,120. The settlement method was payment before delivery. Shenfu issued special VAT invoices for Shanghai, but did not provide proof of payment by Mingyang. During the trial, Shenfu confirmed that part of the payment had not been recovered.

Ye Shuxian, a shareholder of Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd., is the mother of Ding Peikun, a shareholder of Shenfu. Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. is a shareholder of Mingyang, holding 84.1% of its shares.

On February 26, 2010, Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd., commissioned by the Shanghai Branch of Huatai Insurance Agency & Consultant Service Ltd., issued Survey Report No. JX-SH-TB-09184 regarding the cargo damage of imported phenol carried on the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY, concluding: Between October and November 2008, the market price of phenol experienced a sharp decline. Because chemical products are a relatively special type of cargo, we are unable to assess their specific value and possible loss. The notarial certificate (2008) Huzhai Zhengjing Zi No. 5970 issued by the Zhabei Notary Public Office of Shanghai, provided by Shenfu, also showed that at the time of the conclusion of the trade contract on September 23, 2008, the instantaneous market price of phenol nationwide was between RMB 12,220 and 13,000; at the time of vessel discharge on October 24, the instantaneous market price nationwide was between RMB 9,000 and 10,600; at the time Shenfu sent the inquiry letters on November 4, the instantaneous market price nationwide was between RMB 7,000 and 8,200; and at the time Shenfu sold the subject phenol on November 27, the instantaneous market price nationwide was between RMB 5,000 and 6,200.

On September 24, 2008, Shenfu paid an import cargo transportation insurance premium of RMB 11,560.85 to the Shanghai Branch of People's Insurance Company of China for the subject phenol. On October 21, 2008, Shenfu paid import customs duty of RMB 576,175.44 and import VAT of RMB 1,878,855.71 for the subject phenol. On October 22, 2008, the Huangdao Customs of the People's Republic of China issued an import goods declaration form showing: Operating unit: Shenfu; Consignee unit: Shenfu; Goods: phenol, 1,001.53 tons; Use: for self-use by the enterprise, for phenolic resin (electro-wood board); Declaring unit: Qingdao Zhengpai International Logistics Co., Ltd. On October 27, 2008, Shenfu paid an inspection fee of RMB 4,250 to Shanghai Dongfang Tianxiang Inspection Service Co., Ltd. On October 31, 2008, Shenfu paid an inspection fee of RMB 4,000 to SGS-CSTC Standards Technical Services Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch. On January 7, 2009, Shenfu paid an inspection fee of RMB 3,331.25 to Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd.

On October 21, 2010, Qingdao Zhengpai International Logistics Co., Ltd. issued a statement explaining: Under a general trade method, "self-use by the enterprise," since all taxes have been duly paid, it does not affect the import enterprise's ability to sell the imported goods domestically, engage in self-operation, or conduct foreign trade.

To prove that the increase in phenol color caused cargo damage, Shenfu provided a statement from Qingdao Weibang Chemical Co., Ltd.: The production of diphenyl ether requires a phenol color of less than 20 Hazen; a statement from Shandong New Huaxin Chemical Co., Ltd.: The production of salicylic acid requires phenol color to be controlled within 10 Hazen; a statement from Zibo Kewei Chemical Co., Ltd.: The production of tert-butylphenol requires phenol color to be controlled within 10 Hazen; and a statement from Changshu Dongnan Plastic Co., Ltd. and its general manager Wang Keqiang (Chairman of the National Phenolic Resin and Plastics Industry Association): 1. There are several reasons for high phenol color: oxidation by air, iron ions in the tank or storage tank, contamination by other organic substances, or issues with phenol purity. 2. Yellow phenol used to produce phenolic resin results in a dark color, affecting the appearance of the product, and often has an impact on customer acceptance and price.

To support their defenses, Dorval and Hachiman provided the "Expert Opinion on the Impact of Changes in Phenol Indicators" and the "Expert Opinion on the Disposal of Phenol" (hereinafter referred to as "Expert Opinions") prepared by Lin Yanhua, a part-time professor appointed by East China University of Science and Technology. Upon the application of Dorval and Hachiman, Lin Yanhua appeared as an expert witness and was questioned by both parties. Lin Yanhua opined: 1. The subject phenol was discharged into the shore tank in late October 2008, during a period of sharp decline in the domestic phenol market; 2. The main impurities in the subject phenol were trace amounts of colored benzoquinone heavy components formed by oxidation and chemical reaction of phenol; 3. Although the color and moisture indicators of the subject phenol had changed, it still met the requirements of premium grade under "Industrial Synthetic Phenol"; 4. The changes in individual quality indicators of the subject phenol did not affect its sale at the usual market price for premium grade; 5. The subject phenol had no impact when used for producing phenolic resin; 6. The changes in phenol color and moisture indicators could be eliminated through the phenol vacuum distillation tower in the emission recovery system of the bisphenol A production process or in the phenol purification unit of the phenol production plant; 7. The cost of treating the subject phenol using the phenol vacuum distillation tower in the emission recovery system of the bisphenol A production process is as follows: consumption of steam (1 ton of steam per ton of phenol) cost: RMB 200/ton; power consumption cost: RMB 140/ton; phenol loss cost: RMB 60/ton; workshop expenses for manual operations: RMB 50/ton; other enterprise expenses and unforeseen expenses: RMB 90/ton; total: RMB 540/ton (excluding transportation costs).

Shenfu provided a "Statement on Related Costs for Redistillation of Oxidized Phenol Products" from the Sales Office of the Chlor-Alkali Business Unit of Baotou Tomorrow Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tomorrow Technology), which stated: When the quality indicators of phenol products change, they can basically meet usage requirements after redistillation treatment. Related costs (excluding round-trip transportation costs) include: steam cost (12 tons of steam per ton of phenol) RMB 1,440/ton; labor cost RMB 40/ton; phenol loss rate of 5 per thousand; enterprise processing management fee and profit RMB 600/ton. Shenfu provided a freight quotation table from Zibo Shunfuyuan Transport Co., Ltd.: Transport of phenol from Qingdao to Caojing, Shanghai, a distance of 900 km, freight rate RMB 540/ton; transport of phenol from Qingdao to Baotou, a distance of 1,400 km, freight rate RMB 770/ton. Shenfu provided a freight quotation table from Nantong Dongshengtong Chemical Transport Co., Ltd.: Transport of phenol from Qingdao to Shanghai, a distance of 900 km, freight rate RMB 480/ton; transport of phenol from Qingdao to Baotou, a distance of 1,400 km, freight rate RMB 800/ton.

The Qingdao Maritime Court at first instance held that this case is a dispute over cargo damage under a foreign-related contract of carriage of goods by sea. Both parties considered that the laws of the People's Republic of China should apply to this case, so the dispute in this case should be resolved by applying the laws of the People's Republic of China.

Dorval issued an on-board clean bill of lading with the shipper being SUMITOMO DEUTSCHLAND GmbH and is the carrier of the goods under the contract of carriage by sea. Hachiman, as the owner of the M/V GOLDEN TIFFANY which carried the subject goods, is the actual carrier of the goods under the contract of carriage by sea. The bill of lading was endorsed and transferred by the shipper, and Shenfu became the lawful holder of the bill of lading and is the consignee. A contractual relationship for the carriage of goods by sea, evidenced by the bill of lading, was established between Shenfu and Dorval. After taking delivery of the goods, Shenfu claimed compensation from Dorval and Hachiman for the cargo damage. The main issues in dispute in this case are: (1) whether the increase in phenol color constitutes cargo damage; (2) liability for the cargo damage; (3) determination of the amount of cargo loss.

1. Whether the increase in phenol colority constituted cargo damage. The national standard for the molten color of synthetic phenol for industrial use, as determined in the *Chemical Industry Standard Compilation: Organic Chemical Products Volume* published by China Standards Press in 2006, provided that the color standard shall be negotiated between the supplier and the buyer when necessary. The purchase and sale contract between Shenfu Company and Sumitomo Corporation (Hong Kong) Limited stipulated that the phenol colority should not exceed 10 Hazen, which met the requirements of the national standard. According to the relevant inspection reports issued by SGS and Shanghai InspectCommodity Inspection Co., Ltd., the results showed that: before shipment, the phenol colority was less than 5 Hazen; after shipment, the phenol colority was 5 Hazen; before discharge upon the vessel's arrival at Qingdao Port, the phenol colority in tank 7S was 3 Hazen, in tank 7P was 19 Hazen, and in tank 10P was 21 Hazen; after discharge, the phenol colority in Qingdao shore tank T-108 was 12 Hazen. This indicated that the phenol colority had changed to some extent while the goods were under the carrier's custody, and the final mixing of the phenol from three tanks into Qingdao shore tank T-108 resulted in a colority of 12 Hazen for the entire cargo, exceeding the color standard agreed upon by the supplier and buyer. Additionally, Shenfu Company submitted statements from Qingdao Weibang Chemical Co., Ltd., Shandong Xinhua Longxin Chemical Co., Ltd., Zibo Kewei Chemical Co., Ltd., and Changshu Dongnan Plastic Co., Ltd., all of which confirmed that phenol with elevated colority could not be used to produce several downstream products. In summary, the court of first instance found that the increase in phenol colority constituted cargo damage.

Debao Company and Hachiman Company, citing the customs import goods declaration form that stated the phenol was for enterprise self-use and for producing phenolic resin (bakelite), submitted an expert opinion from Lin Yanhua, which argued that the phenol had no impact when used to produce phenolic resin. The court of first instance held that under general trade, imported goods, having paid all normal taxes and being released from customs supervision, could be freely disposed of by the importing enterprise, which did not affect the enterprise's domestic sales, self-use, or foreign trade of the imported goods. Therefore, the phenol in question was not limited to enterprise self-use and production of phenolic resin, and the above claims of Debao Company and Hachiman Company were not supported.

2. Assumption of liability for cargo damage. According to the relevant provisions of the Maritime Law of the PRC, during the period of responsibility from the time the goods are loaded on board until they are discharged, the carrier shall properly and carefully load, handle, stow, carry, keep, care for, and discharge the goods carried. If the goods are lost or damaged during the period of responsibility, the carrier shall be liable for compensation unless there are grounds for exemption. The above provisions regarding the carrier's liability also apply to the actual carrier who performs the entire carriage of the goods. Debao Company, as the carrier of the phenol, and Hachiman Company, as the actual carrier, bear the burden of proving that they have properly and carefully kept and cared for the carried goods during the voyage. The laboratory test results of Shanghai Inspect Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd. (Caojing) on November 5, 2008, for the samples in question showed: the tank sample (taken on August 23, 2008) had a colority of 5 Hazen; before discharge (taken on October 22, 2008): the phenol colority in tank 7S was 3 Hazen, in tank 7P was 19 Hazen, and in tank 10P was 21 Hazen. After arrival at the destination port, the phenol colority had changed significantly compared to the tank sample. Since Hachiman Company failed to provide evidence to prove that it had performed its obligation to properly and carefully keep and care for the goods, nor did it prove that there were grounds for exemption, it shall bear liability for the cargo damage resulting from the phenol colority change. Although Debao Company entrusted the actual carriage of the goods to the actual carrier, as the carrier, it remains responsible for the carriage of the goods. Therefore, for the cargo damage that occurred during the maritime carriage in this case, both the carrier Debao Company and the actual carrier Hachiman Company bear liability for compensation, and Debao Company and Hachiman Company shall bear joint and several liability within the scope of this liability.

3. Determination of the amount of cargo loss. Article 55 of the Maritime Law of the PRC provides: "The amount of compensation for damage to goods shall be calculated based on the difference between the actual value of the goods before and after the damage, or on the cost of repairs." Although Shenfu Company claimed that the amount of compensation should be calculated based on the difference between the actual value of the goods before and after the damage, it was unable to prove that the sale price to Mingyang Company of RMB 4,701,120 (RMB 4,720 per ton) was the actual value of the goods after the damage. This claim was not supported. The court of first instance held that, given the sharp decline in the market price of phenol, it was more reasonable to use the cost of repairs as the depreciation of the goods' own value to calculate the amount of compensation for cargo damage.

The *Expert Opinion* issued by expert Lin Yanhua and the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products* issued by the Supply and Sales Department of the Chlor-Alkali Division of Tomorrow Technology both indicated that through processing by specific procedures, the change in the phenol colority index could be eliminated, substantially meeting usage requirements. From this, it could be determined that the processing by specific procedures constituted the repair process for the phenol, and the cost of such processing should be the repair cost for the phenol. In the *Expert Opinion*, Lin Yanhua proposed that the cost to process the phenol using the phenol vacuum distillation tower in the emission recovery system of the bisphenol A production process was RMB 540 per ton (excluding transportation costs). However, during the trial, he confirmed that this repair cost was calculated only from a technical perspective and had not been verified with relevant chemical enterprises. Therefore, the repair cost proposed by Lin Yanhua had no practical operability or reference value and was not accepted. Tomorrow Technology is a listed company in the chemical raw materials and chemical products manufacturing industry, engaged in the production and sale of related chemical products, with an annual production capacity of 100,000 tons of calcium carbide, 30,000 tons of PVC resin, and 14,000 tons of phenol, among others. The court of first instance held that the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products* issued by the Supply and Sales Department of the Chlor-Alkali Division of Tomorrow Technology was relatively scientific, objective, and reasonable, and could be used as the basis for determining the loss in this case. The repair costs for the phenol were determined as follows: 1. Re-evaporation cost: determined as RMB 2,080 per ton based on the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products*; 2. Phenol loss: since the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products* only determined a loss rate of 5% but did not specify a specific amount, the phenol loss cost was determined as RMB 60 per ton with reference to the loss calculated by expert Lin Yanhua; 3. Transportation cost: based on certificates from Zibo Shunfuyuan Transportation Co., Ltd. and Nantong Dongshengtong Chemical Transportation Co., Ltd., determined as RMB 1,570 per ton for round trip from Qingdao to Baotou. Therefore, the repair cost per ton of phenol was RMB 3,710. Based on the quantity of 1,001.53 tons of the goods in question, the total repair cost for the phenol was RMB 3,715,676.30.

Based on the above analysis, the court of first instance held that Debao Company and Hachiman Company, as the carrier and actual carrier in the maritime carriage of goods, bore joint and several liability for the cargo damage in this case, and should pay Shenfu Company RMB 3,715,676.30 in cargo loss and corresponding interest, with interest calculated from August 12, 2009, the date Shenfu Company filed the lawsuit to assert its rights. The other claims and defenses of Shenfu Company, Debao Company, and Hachiman Company, lacking factual and legal basis, were not supported. Since the compensation liability of Debao Company and Hachiman Company in this case did not exceed the liability limits, the claims of Debao Company and Hachiman Company regarding limitation of liability were not addressed in this case. Pursuant to Articles 46, 48, 55, 60, and 63 of the Maritime Law of the PRC and Article 106 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the PRC, the court of first instance rendered Civil Judgment (2009) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 277 on March 1, 2011, ordering: Debao Company and Hachiman Company to jointly and severally compensate Shenfu Company for cargo loss of RMB 3,715,676.30, plus interest at the bank loan rate for the same period from August 12, 2009, until the date of payment determined by this judgment; and dismissing the other claims of Shenfu Company.

Shenfu Company appealed the judgment of first instance to the Shandong High People's Court: (1) The judgment of first instance erred in some findings of fact. 1. The port of destination for the goods in question was Qingdao, located in the East China region, and the instant market price in East China should have been used; the judgment of first instance inaccurately determined the phenol price based on the instant market price nationwide. 2. Although the judgment of first instance found that Shenfu Company sold the goods to Mingyang Company at RMB 4,720 per ton, it failed to use that price as the actual value of the goods after the damage, which was inconsistent with Shenfu Company's losses. (2) The application of law was improper in part. The judgment of first instance improperly used the cost of repairs to calculate the amount of compensation for the damaged goods, which was an error in the application of law. Shenfu Company requested the court of second instance to correct this in accordance with the law.

Debao Company and Hachiman Company also appealed the judgment of first instance to the Shandong High People's Court: (1) The judgment of first instance erroneously found that the goods had suffered damage. 1. The appellants were not responsible for phenol indicators not recorded in the bill of lading. 2. The national standard for phenol did not require a specific colority, and the phenol in question still met the standard for premium grade. 3. The judgment of first instance failed to address the defense of Debao Company and Hachiman Company that colority is not strictly required for producing phenolic resin, which lacked legal basis. 4. The judgment of first instance, based solely on a statement submitted by Shenfu Company from a commercial company, found that the increase in phenol colority constituted cargo damage without sufficient basis. 5. Shenfu Company did not conduct a tender for the sale of the goods but instead sold them to its affiliate Mingyang Company, in which it held 84.1% equity, and failed to provide payment records or delivery records; obviously, such a transaction could not genuinely prove that the goods had suffered damage. (2) The judgment of first instance erroneously determined the amount of loss. Debao Company and Hachiman Company requested that Shenfu Company's claims be dismissed.

The Shandong High People's Court, upon further investigation at the second instance, found that in the *National Standard for Synthetic Phenol for Industrial Use* (GB/T339-2001), under the technical requirements for synthetic phenol for industrial use, item 3.3 stated: "Molten color: if necessary, shall be negotiated between the supplier and the buyer." The "colority" disputed by the parties in this case refers to the "molten color" in this standard.

Debao Company and Hachiman Company commissioned Shanghai Yue Zhi Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd. to witness the test results of the tank samples taken by Shanghai Inspect Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd. at the time of loading the phenol (Report No. OP2008-1501SH-1).

Other facts found by the court of second instance were consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that this case was a dispute over a foreign-related maritime carriage of goods contract. There were three focal issues in this dispute: (1) whether the change in phenol colority during the maritime carriage constituted cargo damage; (2) if it constituted cargo damage, whether Debao Company and Hachiman Company should bear compensation liability; and (3) how to determine the amount of Shenfu Company's loss.

(1) Regarding whether the change in phenol colority constituted cargo damage. Based on the national standard for synthetic phenol for industrial use, which specifies the technical requirements for phenol, and the statements from multiple chemical companies regarding the relationship between phenol colority and use, it can be seen that colority, in addition to indicators such as appearance, crystallization point, and moisture content, is an important indicator for measuring the quality of phenol. Phenol of different colorities is used to produce different downstream products, and the buyer negotiates with the seller to determine the colority of the phenol according to its own needs. In this case, Shenfu Company and the seller of the goods expressly stipulated in the sales contract that the molten color of the purchased phenol should be below 10 Hazen. However, after transport, the phenol with changed molten color could not meet Shenfu Company's expected needs, and Shenfu Company suffered losses. The change in phenol colority constituted cargo damage.

At the time of loading, the shipper and the carrier sealed samples of the phenol. These sealed samples were carried with the vessel and constituted the basis for the consignee to inspect the quality of the transported phenol. Upon arrival at the destination port, inspection confirmed that among the three cargo tanks carried by the carrier, the goods in one tank were intact, those in another tank had slight colority changes, and those in the third tank showed significant change from the sealed sample. When Shenfu Company refused to take delivery, the carrier, in order to reduce the vessel's losses, issued a statement to Shenfu Company stating that it would bear the losses caused by the mixing of the goods. Shenfu Company received the goods after receiving this statement, and the mixing of the goods caused a change in the colority of the entire cargo, thereby expanding the cargo loss. Subsequently, the parties continuously negotiated, and the carrier requested Shenfu Company to dispose of the goods as soon as possible to avoid further losses. Based on the above process, it can be seen that the carrier and Shenfu Company had already recognized that the goods had suffered losses.

(2) Regarding whether Debao Company and Hachiman Company should bear compensation liability. Although the bill of lading issued by Debao Company contained the notation "the vessel and the master are not aware of the dimensions, weight, specifications, quantity, nature, value, and condition of the goods," according to Article 75 of the Maritime Law of the PRC, for a notation of "unknown" by the carrier on the bill of lading regarding certain characteristics of the goods to be effective, it must state the basis for the suspicion or specify the facts or reasons for the "unknown"; otherwise, such notation is not legally binding on the holder of the bill of lading. In this case, Debao Company did not endorse on the bill of lading the reasons or grounds for its lack of knowledge of the characteristics of the phenol. The fact that Shanghai Inspect Commodity Inspection Co., Ltd. took samples from the tanks after the phenol was loaded and that Debao Company commissioned an insurance surveying company to participate in witnessing the inspection demonstrates that Debao Company should have known the nature, condition, and other characteristics of the phenol. Therefore, the "unknown clause" did not have the effect of exempting the carrier and the actual carrier from liability for compensation for cargo damage. For the cargo damage to the phenol that occurred during the period of transport, Debao Company and Hachiman Company shall jointly and severally compensate Shenfu Company.

Furthermore, regarding the losses that may result from the change in colority of the phenol after discharge, since the carrier issued a statement on October 23, 2008, stating that it would bear the losses caused by the mixing of the goods, Debao Company and Hachiman Company shall also bear joint and several liability for the losses incurred on shore for the goods.

(3) Regarding the determination of the amount of loss. The actual loss of Shenfu Company shall be calculated based on the difference between the actual value of the goods before and after the damage, in accordance with Article 55 of the Maritime Law of the PRC. Since there was expanded loss in this case, the value of the goods after the damage should be calculated based on the value at the time the goods were actually disposed of. The actual value of the goods before the damage was RMB 10,569,474.59. Regarding the actual value of the goods after the damage, the court of second instance held that after taking delivery, Shenfu Company had inquired with several users regarding prices, with sales prices ranging from RMB 4,750/ton to RMB 5,000/ton. During the same period, the instant market prices of phenol nationwide ranged from RMB 4,700/ton to RMB 6,200/ton. Shenfu Company did not sell at the highest inquired price but sold at RMB 4,720/ton to its affiliate Mingyang Company. From the perspective of fair dealing, the price at which Shenfu Company sold the goods to Mingyang Company should not be used as a reference for calculating the value of the goods after the damage. Considering the actual circumstances of the sale process after the quality appraisal of the goods in dispute, it was appropriate to use Shenfu Company's highest quoted price of RMB 5,000/ton as the actual value of the goods after the damage. Therefore, the amount of loss that Debao Company and Hachiman Company should compensate Shenfu Company was RMB 5,589,474.59 (value before damage: RMB 10,569,474.59 - selling price of RMB 5,000/ton x 996 tons), plus corresponding interest.

The court of first instance primarily relied on the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products* submitted by Shenfu Company and, with reference to the *Expert Opinion* submitted by Debao Company and Hachiman Company, determined the repair costs for the phenol. The court of second instance found the following improprieties: First, the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products* submitted by Shenfu Company was intended to prove that the damaged phenol could not meet Shenfu Company's normal use without treatment, not to prove the costs required for re-evaporation of the phenol. That statement did not consider all the costs and losses required for repairing the phenol. Although it was issued by a chemical enterprise that produces and sells chemical products, it was not a scientific, reasonable, or complete statement on the repair costs of the phenol and was insufficient to prove the repair costs. Second, Debao Company and Hachiman Company did not submit sufficient evidence to prove Lin Yanhua's identity as a chemical expert, and Lin Yanhua did not appear in court to be questioned by the parties. After determining that "the repair costs proposed by Lin Yanhua have no practical operability or reference value," the court of first instance then referenced and used the opinion on phenol loss costs from the *Expert Opinion* issued by Lin Yanhua, which was clearly improper. Finally, the *Statement on the Relevant Costs of Re-evaporation after Oxidation of Phenol Products* and the *Expert Opinion* were general statements about the repair costs of phenol; the court could not determine whether the expenses mentioned applied to the specific situation of repairing the phenol in this case from its existing colority to a specific colority. Therefore, it was inappropriate to use these two pieces of evidence as the basis for determining the repair costs of the phenol in this case. Thus, the parties in this case failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove the reasonable expenses required to repair the phenol, and consequently, the court could not calculate Shenfu Company's loss amount based on the "repair costs" provided by law. The judgment of first instance erred in determining the amount of loss.

In summary, the court of second instance held that the judgment of first instance was unclear in some findings of fact, and Shenfu Company's grounds for appeal were valid. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court of second instance rendered Civil Judgment (2011) Lu Min Si Zhong Zi No. 131 on December 7, 2011, ordering: 1. The second item of Civil Judgment (2009) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 277 of Qingdao Maritime Court is affirmed; 2. The first item of Civil Judgment (2009) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 277 of Qingdao Maritime Court is amended as follows: Debao Company and Hachiman Company shall jointly and severally compensate Shenfu Company for losses of RMB 5,589,474.59, plus interest at the bank loan rate for the same period from August 12, 2009, until the date of payment determined by this judgment.

Hachiman Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Hachiman") applied for retrial, alleging: 1. The judgment of the second instance failed to examine and determine the new evidence submitted by Hachiman in the second instance, which violated statutory procedures. 2. The second instance judgment's finding that the cargo was damaged lacked factual basis. The second instance judgment ignored the defense raised by Depo and Hachiman that the carrier was not responsible for matters beyond those recorded in the bill of lading, erroneously found that the carrier should deliver the goods according to the sealed sample, and consequently erroneously found the cargo damage. The national standard for phenol does not require chromaticity; the phenol in question still met the national standard for premium grade. The chromaticity of the phenol in this case was 12 Hazen, and Shenfu had no sufficient evidence to prove that this slightly higher chromaticity would damage the quality of the phenol. The evidence presented by Shenfu concerning the sale of the cargo was not genuine. 3. The method of calculating the cargo loss determined by the second instance judgment lacked factual and legal basis. The calculation method for the loss amount determined by the second instance judgment was erroneous, and the composition of the loss determined was essentially a loss due to market price decline, which does not fall within the scope of liability for damages for breach of contract under the law. Even if cargo damage existed, the loss amount determined by the second instance judgment was significantly higher than the actual loss amount, lacking reasonableness and legal basis. Even if the change in chromaticity could cause loss to Shenfu, Shenfu did not fulfill its duty to mitigate the loss. Even if calculated on the basis of the cargo depreciation rate, the maximum loss amount in this case was only RMB 1,533.40 per ton. The evidence presented by Shenfu concerning the sale of the cargo was not genuine. The second instance judgment's determination that Shenfu could claim interest loss at the loan interest rate lacked legal and factual basis. 4. The second instance judgment did not respond to Hachiman's claim as to whether it was entitled to limit its liability for maritime claims. Hachiman requested this Court to dismiss all of Shenfu's claims.

Shenfu responded, arguing: 1. Hachiman had voluntarily performed the effective judgment of the Shandong High People's Court, but now applied for retrial, which violated Article 13 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC on the principle of good faith, Article 201 on the general prohibition against applying for retrial after a mediation agreement has been performed, and Article 25 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC to the Trial Supervision Procedure, which provides that "if a settlement agreement has been reached in execution and has been fully performed, the review shall be terminated." Therefore, the application should be dismissed according to law. 2. Hachiman's statement that "the second instance judgment failed to examine and determine the new evidence submitted by Hachiman, which violated statutory procedures" was without factual basis. 3. The damage to the subject matter of the dispute was an objective fact; Hachiman's claim that the subject matter of the dispute was not damaged was inconsistent with the facts. 4. Shenfu suffered losses totaling RMB 8,346,527.84 as a result; Hachiman's statement that "the cargo loss amount determined by the second instance judgment lacked factual and legal basis" was inconsistent with the facts and the law. 5. The limitation of liability claimed by Hachiman had no legal basis.

Depo did not submit any opinions, but stated during the court hearing that it agreed with Hachiman's opinions.

Hachiman did not submit new evidentiary materials when applying to this Court for retrial. After the court hearing, Shenfu submitted to this Court its "Product Purchase and Sales Contract" with Zhejiang Liguang Plastic Co., Ltd., the "Product Purchase and Sales Contract" between Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. and Fuzhou Guangsheng Chemical Co., Ltd., and the relevant value-added tax invoices, to prove that the market selling price of phenol notarized by the Shanghai Zhabei Notary Public Office and provided by Shenfu did not include value-added tax.

Hachiman's written challenge to the evidence argued that this evidentiary material was provided by Shenfu after the court hearing and could not be treated as new evidence. On this premise, the "Product Purchase and Sales Contract" between Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. and Fuzhou Guangsheng Chemical Co., Ltd. submitted by Shenfu in this case was dated November 24, 2008, with a price of RMB 8,500 per ton, and the accompanying value-added tax invoice issued by Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. to Fuzhou Guangsheng Chemical Co., Ltd. on December 12, 2008, showed a price including tax of RMB 8,500 per ton. However, in the case of Wuhan Maritime Court (2009) Wu Hai Fa Shang Chu Zi No. 360, the value-added tax invoice issued by Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. to the same entity on December 25, 2008, showed a price including tax of RMB 4,700 per ton. The price differed by almost double within a short period of just over ten days. According to Shenfu's notarized documentation on market price information provided in the original trial, on November 24, 2008, the market price of phenol in East China was RMB 5,800-5,900 per ton, and the price had been declining since August. Assuming Shenfu's statement that the notarized market price information did not include 17% VAT was true, adding 17%, the market price of intact phenol in East China at that time was at most RMB 6,786 per ton. How could Shenfu have sold it at RMB 8,500 per ton? Fuzhou Guangsheng Chemical Co., Ltd. is actually a wholly-owned subsidiary of Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. The above facts, taken together, demonstrate that the contracts between Shenfu and its affiliated companies or business partners were very simple, and Shenfu did not provide evidence of actual payment or delivery to prove the actual occurrence of the transactions. Therefore, this can only prove that either these contracts were all fictitious, or both sets of contracts were not specific. It cannot prove the so-called market price of intact phenol, nor can it prove that the actual selling price of the phenol with increased chromaticity in the case (2009) Wu Hai Fa Shang Chu Zi No. 360 was RMB 4,700 per ton. The sales contracts between Shenfu and its affiliated companies cannot reflect the true selling price of the damaged phenol and cannot be used as a basis for determining the loss.

Regarding the issue of new evidence, this Court holds that Article 44, paragraph 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation stipulates: "If a party provides new evidence in the retrial procedure, it shall be submitted when applying for retrial." This provision requires the applicant for retrial to submit new evidence at the time of applying for retrial, but does not restrict the respondent from submitting relevant evidence to support its defense during the trial of the case. Hachiman did not challenge the authenticity of this evidence itself. Hachiman's claim that this evidentiary material was provided by Shenfu after the court hearing and could not be treated as new evidence lacks a sufficient legal basis.

The price of phenol determined in the "Product Purchase and Sales Contract" between Shenfu and Zhejiang Liguang Plastic Co., Ltd., and the "Product Purchase and Sales Contract" between Shanghai Senfu Industrial Co., Ltd. and Fuzhou Guangsheng Chemical Co., Ltd. submitted by Shenfu cannot prove that the notarized real-time market price of phenol submitted to the court does not include value-added tax. Shenfu's claim that the market price of phenol it submitted does not include value-added tax is not supported by any evidence.

This Court confirms the facts found in the first and second instance judgments. It is additionally found that on November 24, 2008, the market price of phenol in East China was RMB 5,800-5,900 per ton, with an average price of RMB 5,850 per ton. Shenfu claimed to use the East China region phenol market price as the basis for determining the relevant losses, and Hachiman agreed. Shenfu did not submit the market price of phenol in East China on November 27, 2008 (the date of actual sale of the cargo). Both Shenfu and Hachiman agreed to use the price of November 24, 2008, as the basis for determining the facts.

During the retrial of this Court, Shenfu submitted the mediation record of the Shanghai Maritime Court to prove that Hachiman had voluntarily performed the final judgment in this case and then applied for retrial, which violated Article 13 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC on the principle of good faith, Article 201 on the general prohibition against applying for retrial after a mediation agreement has been performed, and Article 25 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC to the Trial Supervision Procedure, which provides that "if a settlement agreement has been reached in execution and has been fully performed, the review shall be terminated." Hachiman argued that the mediation record of the Shanghai Maritime Court concerned the guarantee letter in this case during the trial of a related insurance dispute and the settlement between the parties in that case. In that record, Hachiman did not indicate that it waived its right to apply for retrial. This Court holds that a party's voluntary performance of the payment obligation determined by an effective judgment does not negate its right to apply for retrial. The mediation document of the Shanghai Maritime Court was not made in this case, nor did Hachiman expressly waive its right to apply for retrial in this case. Therefore, Shenfu's argument on this point should not be supported.

This Court holds that this case is a dispute over compensation for cargo damage under a contract of carriage of goods by sea with foreign-related elements. The parties all agreed that the law of the People's Republic of China should apply to this case. Therefore, the courts of first and second instance correctly applied the law of the People's Republic of China as the governing law for this dispute. The Maritime Code of the PRC, as the law regulating maritime transport relations, should apply to this case.

In the transport at issue, Depo issued a clean shipped bill of lading and was the carrier under the contract of carriage of goods by sea. The vessel "Golden Tiffany" owned by Hachiman carried the cargo and was the actual carrier under the contract of carriage of goods by sea. The bill of lading was endorsed and transferred by the shipper, and Shenfu became the lawful holder of the bill of lading and the consignee. A contract of carriage of goods by sea, as evidenced by the bill of lading, was established between Shenfu and Depo. The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) whether the court of second instance violated statutory procedures; (2) whether the judgment of second instance omitted any claims for relief; (3) whether the increase in chromaticity of the phenol constituted cargo damage; (4) the determination of the amount of cargo loss.

(1) Whether the court of second instance violated statutory procedures. Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "The people's court shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, examine and verify evidence comprehensively and objectively." Article 64 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation provides: "Trial personnel shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, examine evidence comprehensively and objectively, and independently judge the probative value and its degree of evidence in accordance with the provisions of law, following the professional ethics of judges, and using logical reasoning and common life experience, and shall publicly state the reasons and results of the judgment." During the second instance, Hachiman submitted documents including the investigation record of the Wuhan Maritime Court concerning Mingtian Technology and background materials from the website of the Ministry of Civil Affairs regarding Wang Keqiang's position in the National Phenolic Resin and Plastics Industry Association. The court of second instance neither listed this set of evidence in its judgment nor publicly stated its conclusion on the determination of this set of evidence. There was indeed a procedural impropriety. However, this procedural defect had no impact on the determination of facts and the judgment result in this case.

(2) Whether the judgment of second instance omitted any claims for relief. Upon verification, Hachiman and Depo raised in their defense reasons at first instance that they were entitled to limit their liability for maritime claims. The court of first instance held that "since the defendant's liability for compensation in this case does not exceed the limitation amount, the defendant's claim regarding the limitation of liability will not be tried in this case." Hachiman and Depo did not again request the limitation of liability for maritime claims in their notices of appeal or oral defenses at second instance. They only raised that they were entitled to limit their liability for maritime claims in their supplementary defense and response to appeal and representation opinions submitted after the second instance hearing. This Court holds that even if Hachiman and Depo's liability for compensation did not exceed their limitation amount for maritime claims, the court should still have tried this defense. Moreover, whether it exceeds the limit must be determined through trial. The court of first instance's failure to try the defense raised by Hachiman and Depo on the ground that it did not exceed the limitation amount was indeed improper. However, Hachiman and Depo did not appeal on this ground. Their claim in the supplementary defense materials submitted after the second instance hearing that they were entitled to limit their liability did not constitute an appeal on the issue of limitation of liability for maritime claims. Therefore, the court of second instance's failure to proactively decide whether they should be entitled to such limitation was not improper.

(3) Whether the increase in chromaticity of the phenol constituted cargo damage. For synthetic phenol for industrial use, although the national standard does not have a mandatory standard for phenol chromaticity, it provides that chromaticity shall be agreed upon by the supplier and buyer when necessary. In this case, the sales contract between Shenfu and Sumitomo Corporation (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. stipulated that the chromaticity of phenol should not exceed 10 Hazen. At the time of loading, the shipper and the carrier sealed a sample of the phenol, which traveled with the cargo and constituted the basis for the consignee's quality inspection of the transported phenol. The existing evidence proves that after the cargo arrived at the port of destination, the chromaticity of the cargo in two of the three holds changed. When Shenfu refused to take delivery, the carrier, in order to minimize losses from vessel detention, issued a statement to Shenfu stating its willingness to bear the losses caused by the mixing of the goods. Therefore, although the cargo in one hold did not change chromaticity, after the phenol from the three holds was mixed and discharged into shore tanks, inspection determined the chromaticity value to be 12 Hazen, which was significantly higher than the chromaticity value of 5 Hazen before and after loading. Based on this, it can be determined that the chromaticity of the phenol changed during the carrier's period of custody, and the phenol suffered actual loss. Depo and Hachiman, as the carrier and actual carrier of the cargo, shall be jointly and severally liable for compensation accordingly. Hachiman's defenses, including that the carrier had no obligation to deliver the cargo according to the sealed sample, that the phenol still met the national standard for premium grade, and that Shenfu did not prove that the slightly higher chromaticity would damage the quality of the phenol, lack factual and legal basis and are not accepted.

(4) Determination of the amount of cargo loss. Article 55 of the Maritime Code of the PRC provides: "The amount of compensation for damage to the goods shall be calculated based on the difference in actual value of the goods before and after the damage, or the cost of repair. The actual value of the goods shall be calculated based on the value of the goods at the time of shipment plus insurance and freight." This provision sets out two methods for calculating the amount of compensation for cargo damage. Since this case does not involve repair costs, the court of second instance did not err in not calculating Shenfu's loss amount based on the "cost of repair" provided by law. Shenfu's loss should be calculated based on "the difference in actual value of the goods before and after the damage," and "the actual value of the goods shall be calculated based on the value of the goods at the time of shipment plus insurance and freight," that is, based on the difference between the CIF value of the goods before and after damage. Due to the long duration of sea transport, the value of goods is susceptible to market fluctuations. The method of calculating the actual value of goods under Article 55 of the Maritime Code of the PRC excludes market price loss, which is consistent with the principle of causation and the principle of reasonable foreseeability in damages for breach of contract.

Between September and November 2008, the domestic market price of phenol experienced significant fluctuations. The second instance judgment used the highest domestic market inquiry price of RMB 5,000 per ton as the actual value of the goods after damage, and subtracted the proceeds from the sale of 996 tons of phenol (calculated at RMB 5,000 per ton) from the value of the goods before damage (the amount Shenfu paid abroad), thereby determining the cargo loss to be RMB 5,589,474.59. The scope of loss of the phenol calculated at this price included both the depreciation loss caused by the change in chromaticity value and the market loss caused by the decline in market price. The market price loss of the phenol does not fall within the scope of loss or damage to goods as defined in the Maritime Code of the PRC, and the carrier is not liable for compensation for such loss.

The calculation of the depreciation rate of the goods due to the change in phenol chromaticity value in this case should be based on the market value of intact goods at the port of destination minus the sales value of the damaged goods, divided by the market value of intact goods. On November 24, 2008, the real-time market price of phenol in East China was RMB 5,800 to 5,900 per ton, with an average price of RMB 5,850 per ton. Both parties agreed to use this price on that day to determine the intact value of the goods on the date Shenfu actually sold the phenol. The second instance judgment considered that Shenfu and Mingyang Company were related companies, and the transaction price between them could not be used as the basis for calculating the loss. However, compared with the average price of intact phenol at the time, the price of RMB 4,720 per ton was not obviously improper. Based on this, the depreciation rate of the goods was calculated as (5850-4720)/5850 = 19.32%. Shenfu's total payment to the foreign party for the cargo was RMB 10,569,474.59, and insurance premium paid was RMB 11,560.85. Shenfu's cargo loss should be (10,569,474.59 + 11,560.85) x 19.32% = RMB 2,044,256.05. Shenfu paid inspection fees of RMB 4,250 to Shanghai Oriental Tianxiang Inspection Service Co., Ltd., RMB 4,000 to SGS-CSTC Standards Technical Services Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch, and RMB 3,331.25 to Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd., totaling RMB 11,581.25, which should be compensated by Hachiman and Depo. The total compensation amounts to RMB 2,055,837.30.

Additionally, Shenfu actually sold 996 tons, but the quantity under the bill of lading was 1,001.53 tons. The court of second instance used 996 tons as the total tonnage of the damaged goods and used 5,000 yuan/ton x 996 tons as the actual value of the goods after damage, which was indeed improper. However, this determination does not affect this Court's determination of facts and the judgment result.

In summary, pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Articles 46, 48, 55, 60, and 63 of the Maritime Code of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2011) Lu Min Si Zhong Zi No. 131 of the Shandong High People's Court is set aside;

2. The civil judgment (2009) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 277 of the Qingdao Maritime Court is set aside;

3. Hachiman Shipping Co., Ltd. and Japan Depo Shipping Co., Ltd. shall jointly and severally compensate Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. for cargo loss in the amount of RMB 2,055,837.30 plus interest (calculated from August 12, 2009, to the date of payment determined in this judgment at the bank loan interest rate for the corresponding period);

4. All other claims of Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

Court acceptance fees of RMB 70,235 for each instance shall be borne by Shanghai Shenfu Chemical Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 52,938.12, and by Hachiman Shipping Co., Ltd. and Japan Depo Shipping Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 17,296.88.

This judgment is final.
